newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Orange to boost European coverage.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Orange to boost European coverage.

text.p: UK mobile telephone operator Orange Plc said it aimed to expand its coverage to almost all of Europe with the introduction of dual band handsets this year.
Finance Director Graham Howe said that the handsets could be launched as early as March but that the more likely date was some time in the second quarter.
Orange's international mobile phones operate on the 1800 MHz frequency, allowing customers to use their handsets in countries such as Germany, France, Switzerland and Hong Kong.
Dual band handsets operate at both 1800 and 900 MHz, enabling them to be used in almost all European countries.

Howe said Orange expected number portability to be introduced in the second half of 1997 and said this would remove a significant barrier preventing the migration of customers from its larger rivals Vodafone and Cellnet.
At present customers cannot bring their cellular number with them if they opt to move from one operator to another.
Howe said that Orange had "the most loyal customer base within the industry", noting that the company's churn rate of 18.6 percent was nearly a third less than the overall average.
He said that Orange's churn rate would be as low as around 13-14 percent if it did not include customers who hand back their mobile phones after an inital 14-day trial period.
He also noted Orange's success in attracting customers to its higher value packages, saying that the company was signing up high volume users.
